solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Supply column tracked vehicle

parts.note: to cater is to supply food or what is needed
a pillar is an upright column

explanation.surface: A military supply column made up of tanks and other tracked vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: A Caterpillar is a tractor or digger running on continuous tracks, named after the trademark track system.

clue.text: What's wrong when wife's right? I'm curious

indicators.note: when the W is made right, the letter is swapped for another

parts.note: askew means awry or wrong

explanation.surface: Someone asks what is wrong when a wife is correct, saying they are curious.
explanation.walkthrough: Change the last W of ASKEW for R. The definition is in the first person: the curious one says 'I'm' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who poses questions out of curiosity is one who asks, so the person speaking describes themself.

clue.text: Hermit describes opening of Catch 22

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round, so the hermit goes around the letter

parts.note: the Essenes were an ascetic Jewish sect living apart in the wilderness

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here of Catch

explanation.surface: A recluse talks about the start of Heller's novel Catch-22.
explanation.walkthrough: '22' is not part of the novel's title but points to 22-down, whose answer means the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The cross-reference leads to a word for the vital nature of a thing, a synonym of essence.

clue.text: Dearest dad's bad mood

parts.note: pop is a word for dad; the 's is read as 'is'
a pet is a fit of sulking

explanation.surface: A child tells their dearest that dad is in a sulk.
explanation.definitionFit: Poppet is a British term of endearment like darling or sweetheart.

clue.text: Proud, working for Scottish Herald

parts.note: lordly means haughty or proud
on means working, as of a machine switched on

explanation.surface: A proud man stands in for a Scottish newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Herald is a Glasgow newspaper, which is the surface's misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord Lyon King of Arms is Scotland's chief heraldic officer.

clue.text: Areas without music house Native Americans

indicators.note: without means outside, so the areas go round the music

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area, so two areas give two As
rap is a style of music

explanation.surface: Districts lacking any music are home to Native American peoples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: A and A go round RAP.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arapaho are a people of the American plains.

clue.text: Strip search thus might be tricky work

definitions.text: Strip search thus might be tricky work

parts.words: Strip search thus might be tricky work
parts.note: a search of the Gaza Strip made without eyes would be tricky; the answer is also a work, a novel by Aldous Huxley

explanation.surface: A security strip search could be awkward to carry out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip search' suggests airport security, but the strip is the Gaza Strip.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeless in Gaza is Huxley's 1936 novel, its title taken from Milton's Samson Agonistes.

clue.text: Venus possibly feeling early morning sun

parts.note: will is desire or inclination, a feeling
1 a.m. is early morning, written as I AM

explanation.surface: Someone senses the planet Venus near the sun before dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: Venus seems to be the planet; it is Venus Williams.
explanation.definitionFit: Venus Williams is a US tennis champion, one example of a bearer of the surname.

clue.text: Serving soldiers meet with resistance?

parts.note: soldiers are fingers of toast dipped in a soft egg; a serving that is solid would resist them

explanation.surface: Troops on active duty come up against an enemy resistance movement.
explanation.walkthrough: Soldiers are a British breakfast item, strips of toast dunked into a runny egg yolk.
explanation.definitionFit: A boiled egg cooked until solid gives the toast fingers nowhere to dip, so they meet resistance.

clue.text: My pick occasionally cuts very well

indicators.note: one piece cuts into the other, so the picked letters go inside

parts.note: 'very well' is a form of agreement, like saying yes

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so every other letter of pick is taken

explanation.surface: Someone admires how neatly their chosen pickaxe slices through things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive, but it is the exclamation of surprise; 'occasionally' takes every other letter of pick, and 'cuts' sends them into the phrase for very well.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise or alarm, so one interjection swaps for the other.

clue.text: A head beginning to pass port around with bread

indicators.note: the beginning to a word is its first letter, here of pass
turned around means the port's name is read backwards

parts.note: Acre is a port in northern Israel
pitta or pita is a flat Middle Eastern bread

explanation.surface: Instructions for a dinner party: send the port round and serve bread.
explanation.walkthrough: Acre is a port in Israel; 'around' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means for each person, which is what 'a head' means in prices such as five pounds a head.

clue.text: A yell rang out, coming from the throat

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone let out a shout that came from deep in the throat.
explanation.definitionFit: The larynx is the voice box in the throat, so a sound produced there is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Controlled by software, evidently upset

parts.note: AI, artificial intelligence, is a kind of software
led means guided or controlled

explanation.surface: A device run by software is obviously malfunctioning.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as AI-LED the answer means 'controlled by software'; as one word it is the past tense meaning troubled.
explanation.definitionFit: Ailed is the past tense of ail, to trouble or afflict, so it can stand for upset as a verb in the past.

clue.text: Wept, finding B&B in small dictionary

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: in tells us the pair of letters is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: the OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
the letters B and B written out

explanation.surface: Someone cried on discovering their bed-and-breakfast listed in a pocket dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the pair of Bs inside the Oxford English Dictionary's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: To sob is to cry with convulsive breaths, so its past tense matches wept.

clue.text: A lobster camouflaged as fish

indicators.note: something camouflaged is disguised, so the letters are rearranged to hide them

explanation.surface: A lobster disguises itself as a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloaters are herrings cured whole by salting and smoking, so they are a kind of fish.

clue.text: Racial problems for American state?

parts.note: racial matters concern skin colour, spelt color in American English
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A question about whether a US state has a problem with race.
explanation.walkthrough: The American spelling COLOR is needed, which the question mark and 'American' allow.
explanation.definitionFit: Colorado is one of the fifty states of the USA, in the Rocky Mountains.

clue.text: Put to death or turned into target for abuse

indicators.note: into puts the turned word inside the other
abuse means misuse, so the letters of target are mistreated and rearranged
turned means the little word or is reversed

explanation.surface: Someone was either executed or became a target of abuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' gives RO, which goes into GARTTE, the anagram of TARGET from 'for abuse'.
explanation.definitionFit: To garrotte is to execute by strangling, often with a wire or iron collar.

clue.text: Invulnerable as band appearing in fringe

indicators.note: a band appearing inside another piece tells us the answer is an instruction that puts a ring in something

parts.note: the word fringe is RING, a band, wrapped in FE, the symbol for iron: a band clad in iron

explanation.surface: A band performing at the Edinburgh Fringe is described as invincible.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as instructions, IRON (FE) CLAD round a band (RING), and you build the word fringe. The Fringe is the Edinburgh arts festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Something armoured all over with metal plates cannot be harmed, hence the figurative sense of impossible to break down.

clue.text: Tea's ready — I'll get the bread

parts.note: cha is a word for tea; the 's is read as 'is'
off pat means learnt and ready to go

explanation.surface: Tea is served, and someone offers to fetch the bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is an unleavened flatbread from South Asia.

clue.text: Having split, withstand betrayer

parts.note: split as with + stand: W is the abbreviation for with
the stand half: an easel is a painter's stand

explanation.surface: After a split, someone resists the person who betrayed them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having split' tells you to break 'withstand' into WITH (W) and STAND (EASEL).
explanation.definitionFit: A weasel is slang for a sneaky, treacherous person who lets others down.

clue.text: I put out erotic novel — see cuts

indicators.note: cuts means it slices into the rearranged letters
novel means new, so the letters are given a new arrangement

parts.note: V is the abbreviation of vide, Latin for see

explanation.surface: An author says they published an erotic novel, with some cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is in the first person, spoken by the one who throws people out. 'novel' rearranges EROTIC, and V goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An evictor is one who turns tenants out, so 'I put out' is the evictor speaking.

clue.text: Bottle of solution in alcohol

definitions.meaning: bottle is British slang for courage or nerve
a solution of a substance in alcohol, such as camphor dissolved in alcohol

explanation.surface: A bottle containing some liquid mixed with alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' looks like a container but is British slang for nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage is also called spirit, and in pharmacy a spirit is an alcoholic solution of a volatile substance.

clue.text: Must leave one following empty threat

parts.note: to go is to leave

indicators.note: an empty word loses its inside, keeping only the outer letters of threat

parts.note: A means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: Someone has to go after an idle threat has been made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' just places A after the emptied threat.
explanation.definitionFit: Gotta is the informal contraction of 'got to', meaning have to or must.

clue.text: One selling space station returned with rocket

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

indicators.note: returned means the station's name comes back reading backwards

parts.note: Mir was the Soviet and Russian space station
and means with, together

explanation.surface: An advertising salesperson came back from a space station on a rocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' makes RIM of MIR. 'Rocket' looks like the spaceship but is British slang for a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocket in British slang is a severe scolding, the same as a formal rebuke.

clue.text: Furthermore, footballers turned up

indicators.note: turned means the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: too means furthermore, also
the FA is the Football Association

explanation.surface: What's more, the football team arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' seems one phrase meaning arrived, but 'up' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Afoot means happening or going on, as in 'what's up?'.

clue.text: Prophet put pig on cross

indicators.note: in a down light 'on' would place one piece over another; here it puts the pig after the cross

parts.note: a zo or dzo is a cross between a yak and a domestic cow
a roaster is a young pig fit for roasting

explanation.surface: An order to put a pig onto a cross, like a spit roast.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoroaster, also Zarathustra, was the ancient Persian prophet who founded Zoroastrianism.

clue.text: Crowd's run away, leaving band

indicators.note: something run away is gone, so the letter goes out of the word

parts.note: a throng is a crowd; the 's is read as 'has'
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A crowd has dispersed, abandoning a music group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' seems to be a music group, but it is a strip of material.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is a narrow strip of leather used as a strap or lace.

clue.text: One minister comes in to see executive

indicators.note: comes in places these pieces inside the other

parts.note: to date or be seeing someone is to go out with them
I is the Roman numeral one
a rector is a parish minister in the Church

explanation.surface: A clergyman enters to meet a company executive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to see' means to go out with someone, a sense the surface hides behind meeting the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A directorate is a board of directors, the executive body of an organisation.
